description: Routes the input to one of the linked nodes using an LLM

llm_provider_id.description: The configured LLM service provider this node calls, e.g. the team's OpenAI account.
llm_provider_id.title: LLM Model

llm_provider_model_id.description: The model to call, e.g. gpt-4o. Must belong to the same provider type as `llm_provider_id` -- an OpenAI provider cannot run an Anthropic model.
llm_provider_model_id.title: Llm Provider Model Id

llm_model_parameters.description: Generation settings passed to the model, such as `temperature`. Which keys are accepted depends on the model; leave empty to use its defaults.
llm_model_parameters.title: Llm Model Parameters

history_type.title: PipelineChatHistoryTypes
history_type.description: Which past messages to put in the prompt. `none` sends only the current input; `node` remembers just this node's own turns; `named` shares one history between every node set to the same `history_name`; `global` uses the participant's whole conversation.

history_name.description: The shared history to read and write. Only used when `history_type` is `named`.
history_name.title: History Name

history_mode.title: PipelineChatHistoryModes
history_mode.description: How to shrink history that outgrows its limit: `summarize` replaces old messages with a summary, `truncate_tokens` drops them to fit `user_max_token_limit`, and `max_history_length` keeps only the most recent `max_history_length` messages.

user_max_token_limit.description: Maximum number of tokens before messages are summarized or truncated.
user_max_token_limit.title: Token Limit

max_history_length.description: Chat history will only keep the most recent messages up to this limit.
max_history_length.title: Max History Length

name.description: Identifies the node within its pipeline. Another node reaches this one's result through `temp_state.outputs.<name>`, so renaming it breaks any template that does.
name.title: Node Name

keywords.description: The routes this node can take, one per output. Uppercased and deduplicated on save. Entry `i` is served by output handle `output_i`, so adding, removing or reordering keywords rewires the node's outgoing edges.
keywords.title: Keywords

default_keyword_index.description: Position in `keywords` to fall back to when no route matches. Must be a valid index into `keywords`.
default_keyword_index.title: Default Keyword Index

tag_output_message.description: Tag the output message with the selected route
tag_output_message.title: Tag Output Message

prompt_mode.title: Prompt Mode
prompt_mode.description: How the router's prompt is built. `standard` builds it from the routes and their `route_descriptions`; `standard_with_context` adds `custom_context` to that; `custom` sends `prompt` instead. A router saved without this setting reads as `custom`.

custom_context.description: Instructions added to the standard prompt in `standard_with_context` mode, such as which route to prefer in a borderline case. Takes the same template variables as `prompt`.
custom_context.title: Additional Context

prompt.default: You are an extremely helpful router
prompt.description: Instructions telling the LLM how to choose between `keywords`, used in `custom` mode. The model is constrained to return one of them, so describe when each applies rather than asking for free text. The only template variables available are `{participant_data}`, `{temp_state}`, `{session_state}`, `{routes}` and `{routes_list}`, in single braces. `{routes}` lists each keyword with its entry in `route_descriptions`; `{routes_list}` lists the keywords alone.
prompt.title: Prompt

prompt_template_version.description: The version of the standard prompt this router uses in `standard` and `standard_with_context` modes. New routers get the latest version. A router keeps its version until it is changed, so a newer standard prompt never changes how an existing router routes.
prompt_template_version.title: Prompt Template Version

route_descriptions.description: What each route is for, keyed by keyword. Rendered into the prompt by the `{routes}` variable. Keys are uppercased on save. An entry for a keyword not in `keywords` is kept but not used.
route_descriptions.title: Route Descriptions

title: RouterNode
